title: Linked List Cycle II
keyIdea: Same Floyd trick as LC 287, on a real linked list. Meet inside the loop, send one pointer back to head, move both 1 step: they meet at the cycle's first node. Unlike 287, the list might have no cycle, so check for NULL.

approaches.name: Brute force (hash set)
approaches.idea: Walk the list and remember every node. The first node you see twice is where the cycle starts. Reach NULL → no cycle.
approaches.why: Each node is visited once and stored once in the set.

approaches.name: Floyd's cycle detection
approaches.idea: fast moves 2, slow moves 1. If fast hits NULL there's no cycle. If they meet, reset fast to head and move both 1 step until they meet again.
approaches.why: Phase 1 takes at most about n steps, phase 2 exactly L steps. Only two pointers, no extra memory.

quiz.q: Why does the loop check both fast != NULL and fast->next != NULL?
options: fast jumps two nodes; if fast->next is NULL then fast->next->next would crash

quiz.q: In phase 2, how far does fast move each iteration?
The cycle starts at head (L = 0). What happens right after fast = head?
options: fast == slow already, so the while loop is skipped and head is returned
fast needs one full lap first
